title: GeoChat: Grounded Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing
venue: CVPR 2024
takeaway: Baseline RS chat model (RGB only, 7B); reuse its task-token routing and dataset-to-instruction recipe, but do not trust VLM-emitted boxes (about 10.6% referring detection acc@0.5)

title: EarthGPT: A Universal Multi-modal Large Language Model for Multi-sensor Image Comprehension in Remote Sensing Domain
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), 2024
takeaway: MMRS-1M (optical, SAR, infrared) is a ready seed for LoRA data; its pixel-level weakness supports keeping masks in a separate, non-LLM head

title: EarthDial: Turning Multi-sensory Earth Observations to Interactive Dialogues
venue: CVPR 2025
takeaway: Closest prior work (4B, open weights, Sentinel-1 VH plus S2 plus change); top LoRA base candidate, and SatClip must beat it on provenance, calibration and abstention

title: SkyEyeGPT: Unifying Remote Sensing Vision-Language Tasks via Instruction Tuning with Large Language Model
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, vol. 221, pp. 64-77 (2025); arXiv 2024
takeaway: Lean frozen-encoder plus linear-projector design suits a CPU-first prototype; expect degradation from aerial to 10 m Sentinel resolution

title: LHRS-Bot: Empowering Remote Sensing with VGI-Enhanced Large Multimodal Language Model
venue: ECCV 2024
takeaway: Copy the OpenStreetMap/VGI auto-captioning trick for cheap Indian training pairs and multiple-choice evals; check rural OSM sparsity

title: RSGPT: A Remote Sensing Vision Language Model and Benchmark
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, vol. 224, pp. 272-286 (2025); arXiv preprint 2307.15266 (2023)
takeaway: Copy RSICap's rich human-caption style and build a small Indian RSIEval-like test set; beat it on grounding and confidence

title: TEOChat: A Large Vision-Language Assistant for Temporal Earth Observation Data
venue: ICLR 2025
takeaway: Use its temporal task taxonomy for before/after queries; too heavy for CPU and has no SAR or calibration, which SatClip adds

title: RemoteCLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model for Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), 2024
takeaway: Default CPU zero-shot and retrieval backbone; validate on Indian Sentinel-2 and calibrate its similarity scores before abstention

title: RS5M and GeoRSCLIP: A Large Scale Vision-Language Dataset and A Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), 2024, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2024.3449154
takeaway: Bake off GeoRSCLIP against RemoteCLIP; its PEFT results back the LoRA plan, but keep eval captions human-written

title: SkyScript: A Large and Semantically Diverse Vision-Language Dataset for Remote Sensing
venue: AAAI 2024 (Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 38, no. 6)
takeaway: Reuse the OSM-to-caption trick for Indian training pairs, watching for sparse rural OSM coverage; add SkyCLIP to the backbone bake-off

title: RSVQA: Visual Question Answering for Remote Sensing Data
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2020.2988782
takeaway: Sentinel-2 VQA baseline to evaluate on first; copy OSM-template QA generation and always run a blind (no-image) baseline to expose language bias

title: VRSBench: A Versatile Vision-Language Benchmark Dataset for Remote Sensing Image Understanding
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track
takeaway: Reference LoRA recipe and human-verified QA design, but VHR optical only and grounding about 57% at IoU 0.5, so masks need a dedicated segmenter

title: Good at captioning, bad at counting: Benchmarking GPT-4V on Earth observation data
venue: CVPR 2024 Workshops (EarthVision), pp. 7839-7849; also presented at ICLR 2024 ML4RS workshop
takeaway: Let the VLM caption and explain but route counts, boxes and damage to dedicated instruments; GPT-4V got about 0.16 mIoU on localization

title: GEOBench-VLM: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Geospatial Tasks
venue: ICCV 2025 (per official GitHub README)
takeaway: Best open VLM reaches only about 42% MCQ accuracy on geospatial tasks, which justifies tool grounding plus abstention; reuse its task taxonomy

title: FloodNet: A High Resolution Aerial Imagery Dataset for Post Flood Scene Understanding
takeaway: Borrow the flood question taxonomy rescaled to 10 m Sentinel, and guard against flood versus permanent water confusion with a reference layer

title: Exploring Models and Data for Remote Sensing Image Caption Generation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), vol. 56, pp. 2183-2195, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2017.2776321
takeaway: Use its caption annotation rules as SatClip's caption style guide; do not trust BLEU or CIDEr without a grounding check

title: BigEarthNet-MM: A Large Scale Multi-Modal Multi-Label Benchmark Archive for Remote Sensing Image Classification and Retrieval
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine (GRSM), 2021 (venue as given in brief; not shown on the fetched arXiv page)
takeaway: Use BigEarthNet-pretrained S1/S2 encoders next to RemoteCLIP, expose only labels separable at 10 m, and measure the Europe-to-India domain gap

title: SEN12MS: A Curated Dataset of Georeferenced Multi-Spectral Sentinel-1/2 Imagery for Deep Learning and Data Fusion
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences, vol. IV-2/W7, pp. 153-160, DOI 10.5194/isprs-annals-IV-2-W7-153-2019
takeaway: Paired global S1/S2 data plus a recipe for building an Indian SAR-optical set; its coarse MODIS labels suit weak supervision only

title: Multisensor Data Fusion for Cloud Removal in Global and All-Season Sentinel-2 Imagery
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2020.3024744 (online 2020, issue 2021)
takeaway: SEN12MS-CR is the monsoon cloud-gap test set; use cloud masks to choose between optical, SAR and abstaining, never present filled pixels as observed

title: Cloud removal in Sentinel-2 imagery using a deep residual neural network and SAR-optical data fusion
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, vol. 166, pp. 333-346, DOI 10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2020.05.013
takeaway: Baseline for SAR-guided cloud filling; flag reconstructed areas and skip indices there; too heavy for per-query CPU use

title: SARChat-Bench-2M: A Multi-Task Vision-Language Benchmark for SAR Image Interpretation
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2502.08168, v5 March 2025)
takeaway: About 2M SAR image-text pairs and released checkpoints give a SAR baseline, but imagery is mostly high-res targets, so test on Indian Sentinel-1

title: Sen1Floods11: A Georeferenced Dataset to Train and Test Deep Learning Flood Algorithms for Sentinel-1
venue: CVPR Workshops 2020 (pp. 210-211)
takeaway: Standard Sentinel-1 flood baseline (11 events, none in India); keep an Otsu VH threshold as a sanity check and build an Indian held-out test

title: Remote Sensing ChatGPT: Solving Remote Sensing Tasks with ChatGPT and Visual Models
venue: IGARSS 2024 (arXiv comment says submitted; README indicates acceptance)
takeaway: Simple LLM plan-and-call-tools loop with no quantitative evaluation; copy the loop with an open CPU LLM and add confidence propagation and abstention

title: GeoLLM-Engine: A Realistic Environment for Building Geospatial Copilots
venue: CVPR 2024 Workshops (EarthVision)
takeaway: GPT-4 agent success fell as tool chains grew longer; keep SatClip plans short and fixed and track tool-call correctness

title: RS-LLaVA: A Large Vision-Language Model for Joint Captioning and Question Answering in Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: Remote Sensing (MDPI), 16(9), 1477
takeaway: LoRA recipe and released 7B checkpoint are a fine-tune starting point; its ungrounded, confidence-free output is the gap SatClip fills

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
venue: ICML 2017
takeaway: Modern deep nets are overconfident; fit one temperature on held-out data to calibrate any score, report ECE and a reliability diagram, accuracy is unchanged

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
venue: NeurIPS 2017 (NIPS 2017)
takeaway: Pick the abstention threshold from a target risk with a statistical guarantee on held-out data; trading coverage for reliability (2% ImageNet top-5 error at about 60% coverage)

title: Uncertainty Sets for Image Classifiers using Conformal Prediction
venue: ICLR 2021 (Spotlight)
takeaway: RAPS wraps any classifier to output label sets with a finite-sample coverage guarantee (for example 90%), with sets often 5 to 10 times smaller than a Platt-scaling baseline

title: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
venue: EMNLP 2023
takeaway: LVLMs often claim objects that are not there, especially frequent or co-occurring ones; POPE's yes/no probing with adversarial negatives is a cheap template for SatClip's hallucination tests

title: Reliable Visual Question Answering: Abstain Rather Than Answer Incorrectly
venue: ECCV 2022
takeaway: Softmax-thresholded VQA models answer under 7.5% of questions at 1% risk; a learned multimodal selector raises coverage from 6.8% to 15.6%, and Effective Reliability penalises wrong answers more than abstentions

title: Enabling Calibration In The Zero-Shot Inference of Large Vision-Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2303.12748, v2 April 2023)
takeaway: CLIP zero-shot scores are miscalibrated; one temperature learned per CLIP model on an auxiliary set transfers across prompts and datasets, so calibrate RemoteCLIP once and reuse

title: Spatial-Aware Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Hyperspectral Image Classification
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2409.01236, v2 October 2024)
takeaway: Conformal prediction works for per-pixel RS classification, and smoothing non-conformity scores over spatial neighbours gives smaller sets at the same guaranteed coverage; apply it to SatClip masks

title: RSHallu: Dual-Mode Hallucination Evaluation for Remote-Sensing Multimodal Large Language Models with Domain-Tailored Mitigation
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2602.10799, February 2026)
takeaway: RS VLMs answer hallucination-free only about 36% to 69% of the time on RSHalluEval, including errors about modality and resolution; strong evidence that SatClip's VLM must not produce measurements

title: A Theoretical Framework for Unsupervised Change Detection Based on Change Vector Analysis in the Polar Domain
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), vol. 45, no. 1, pp. 218-236, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2006.885408
takeaway: Formal basis for optical change vector analysis: magnitude says whether something changed, direction says what kind; use it as the transparent Sentinel-2 change instrument instead of a black-box network

title: Urban Change Detection for Multispectral Earth Observation Using Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: IGARSS 2018 (IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium, Valencia)
takeaway: OSCD is the small but standard Sentinel-2 urban change benchmark (24 pairs, 13 bands, pixel labels); use it to calibrate optical change thresholds, not to train large models

title: An unsupervised approach based on the generalized Gaussian model to automatic change detection in multitemporal SAR images
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), vol. 43, no. 4, pp. 874-887, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2004.842441
takeaway: Canonical SAR change recipe (despeckle, log-ratio, automatic threshold from a fitted two-class model); adopt it nearly as-is for Sentinel-1 change with the fitted model doubling as a confidence source

title: A Spatial-Temporal Attention-Based Method and a New Dataset for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
venue: Remote Sensing (MDPI), 12(10), 1662, DOI 10.3390/rs12101662
takeaway: LEVIR-CD (637 pairs, 0.5 m, Texas buildings) became the default CD benchmark; useful for language templates and model comparison but not for calibrating 10 m Sentinel instruments

title: Remote Sensing Image Change Detection with Transformers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), 2021, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2021.3095166
takeaway: Strong, small (about 3.5M params) learned CD baseline at 89.3 F1 on LEVIR-CD but only 69.3 on DSIFN; a cross-check at most, never the source of SatClip's number

title: xBD: A Dataset for Assessing Building Damage from Satellite Imagery
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:1911.09296 (related version in CVPR 2019 Workshops; venue not re-confirmed)
takeaway: Largest pre/post building damage set (850k polygons, 19 events, sub-0.8 m); its baseline damage F1 of about 0.27 shows per-building damage is out of reach for 10 m Sentinel, so SatClip should abstain on it

title: Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning With Dual-Branch Transformers: A New Method and a Large Scale Dataset
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS), vol. 60, 5633520, DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2022.3218921
takeaway: LEVIR-CC (10,077 pairs, 50,385 captions, half no-change) is the standard change-captioning set; good template data for SatClip's explanation layer, but captions carry no measured quantities

title: Kuro Siwo: 33 billion m² under the water. A global multi-temporal satellite dataset for rapid flood mapping
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, vol. 37)
takeaway: Expert-labelled Sentinel-1 pre/post flood set (43 events, CC BY, separates flood from permanent water); the best calibration set for SatClip's SAR flood change instrument, though Asia is underrepresented

title: Flood inundation mapping- Kerala 2018; Harnessing the power of SAR, automatic threshold detection method and Google Earth Engine
venue: PLOS ONE, 15(8): e0237324, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0237324
takeaway: Otsu on Sentinel-1 VV (Lee 5x5) mapped the Kerala August 2018 flood at about 94.7% OA (kappa 0.87 to 0.88) against Sentinel-2; a ready Indian validation event and baseline for our SAR water instrument

title: Google Earth Engine-Based Identification of Flood Extent and Flood-Affected Paddy Rice Fields Using Sentinel-2 MSI and Sentinel-1 SAR Data in Bihar State, India
venue: Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing, 50, 791-803, DOI 10.1007/s12524-021-01487-3
takeaway: Bihar monsoon 2020: S1 plus S2 in GEE mapped about 7,019 sq km submerged and water standing on paddy for 50 to 65 days; a model for flood-on-crop questions, but method details sit behind a paywall

title: High resolution paddy rice maps in cloud-prone Bangladesh and Northeast India using Sentinel-1 data
venue: Scientific Data, 6, Article 26, DOI 10.1038/s41597-019-0036-3
takeaway: Sentinel-1 VH time series plus random forest mapped 2017 paddy at 10 m in Northeast India and Bangladesh per season (Boro, Aus, Aman) at 94 to 98% OA; reuse as a crop mask and adopt VH time series for rice questions

title: Radar versus optical: The impact of cloud cover when mapping seasonal surface water for health applications in monsoon-affected India
venue: PLOS ONE, 20(1): e0314033, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0314033
takeaway: In Western Ghats districts, July to August cloud cover averaged about 90%, leaving roughly a quarter of surface water unmapped in the optical JRC product; Sentinel-1 VV recovered it, so monsoon questions must default to SAR

title: Flood Affected Area Atlas of India - Satellite based study
venue: Official technical document, NRSC/ISRO (released 11 March 2023), hosted on NDEM
takeaway: The official Indian baseline: 25 years (1998 to 2022) of IRS and foreign optical/SAR flood layers, SAR water by variable thresholding, validated by state agencies; SatClip should complement it, not compete

title: Google Earth Engine: Planetary-scale geospatial analysis for everyone
venue: Remote Sensing of Environment, 202, 18-27, DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2017.06.031
takeaway: The reference cloud EO platform: a hosted multi-sensor catalogue with lazy, tile-parallel evaluation; most Indian SAR flood papers run on it, but it is closed and code-centric, so SatClip should match its ergonomics on open STAC plus COG

title: The Australian Geoscience Data Cube - Foundations and lessons learned
venue: Remote Sensing of Environment, 202, 276-292, DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2017.03.015
takeaway: Open Data Cube foundations: analysis-ready, provenance-tracked data plus a light index and open (Apache 2.0) code make time series trustworthy; SatClip should copy the provenance discipline, not the heavy ingest

title: OGC Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF Standard
venue: OGC Implementation Standard 21-026, version 1.0 (approved 8 May 2023, published 14 July 2023)
takeaway: COG 1.0 formalises tiled GeoTIFFs with overviews and headers up front, served over HTTP range requests; this is what lets SatClip read only the district window from a Sentinel scene on a CPU worker

title: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC) Specification
venue: Standard specification (v1.1.0, released 11 September 2024; v1.0.0 released 25 May 2021)
takeaway: STAC is the common search language of public EO catalogues (Item, Catalog, Collection, API); SatClip should search with STAC API and record STAC Item IDs and hrefs in every receipt

title: SatMAE: Pre-training Transformers for Temporal and Multi-Spectral Satellite Imagery
venue: NeurIPS 2022
takeaway: The founding MAE recipe for multispectral and temporal satellite data; treat it as background and baseline, not as a SatClip runtime component

title: Prithvi-EO-2.0: A Versatile Multi-Temporal Foundation Model for Earth Observation Applications
venue: arXiv preprint (December 2024); peer-reviewed venue not confirmed
takeaway: Open NASA/IBM multi-temporal HLS model with flood and crop fine-tune recipes; best GPU candidate for a learned second opinion next to SatClip's optical instruments, not a CPU default

title: SkySense: A Multi-Modal Remote Sensing Foundation Model Towards Universal Interpretation for Earth Observation Imagery
venue: CVPR 2024
takeaway: Billion-parameter optical plus SAR plus time model showing fusion helps; a ceiling to cite, but non-commercial weights and size rule it out for SatClip

title: SSL4EO-S12: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal, Multi-Temporal Dataset for Self-Supervised Learning in Earth Observation
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine, vol. 11, no. 3, pp. 98-106, 2023
takeaway: Open Sentinel-1/2 pretraining corpus with small ResNet50 and ViT-S weights in TorchGeo; the most CPU-friendly source of Sentinel-native features for SatClip experiments

title: CROMA: Remote Sensing Representations with Contrastive Radar-Optical Masked Autoencoders
venue: NeurIPS 2023
takeaway: MIT-licensed radar plus optical encoder trained on Sentinel-1/2; best candidate for a learned SAR feature cross-check next to SatClip's Otsu water instrument

title: Neural Plasticity-Inspired Multimodal Foundation Model for Earth Observation
venue: arXiv preprint (v1 March 2024, v3 October 2025); peer-reviewed venue not confirmed
takeaway: One encoder for any band set via wavelength conditioning (DOFA); lets SatClip use a single learned backbone for both Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 in experiments

title: Clay Foundation Model
venue: Technical documentation (no peer-reviewed paper found; docs describe release v1.5)
takeaway: Apache-licensed multi-sensor embedding model with precomputed embeddings; useful for similarity search and change hints in SatClip, never as the source of reported numbers

title: SpectralGPT: Spectral Remote Sensing Foundation Model
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), 2024 (accepted per arXiv comment)
takeaway: 3D spatial-spectral MAE for Sentinel-2 with change detection results; reference for spectral-aware features, but GPL licence and size keep it out of SatClip core

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
venue: ICLR 2022 (arXiv June 2021)
takeaway: The adapter method behind SatClip's VLM fine-tuning pipeline; merge adapters for zero-latency CPU inference and keep the base weights frozen and versioned

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
venue: NeurIPS 2023
takeaway: 4-bit base plus LoRA adapters makes VLM fine-tuning fit on one consumer or free-tier GPU; SatClip's LoRA pipeline should offer a QLoRA mode

title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
venue: MLSys 2024 (Best Paper Award); arXiv June 2023
takeaway: Calibration-light 4-bit weight quantization that preserves accuracy and works for multimodal models; a strong way to shrink SatClip's VLM after LoRA merge

title: MobileCLIP: Fast Image-Text Models through Multi-Modal Reinforced Training
venue: CVPR 2024
takeaway: Small, fast CLIP models via reinforced training; a CPU-friendly alternative encoder for SatClip's zero-shot land cover instrument if licence and accuracy on Sentinel-2 check out

title: SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models
venue: arXiv preprint (April 2025); peer-reviewed venue not confirmed
takeaway: Fully open 256M to 2.2B VLMs built for edge devices; the most realistic CPU base for SatClip's question parser and explainer, fine-tuned with LoRA

title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
venue: NIPS 2014 Deep Learning Workshop (arXiv:1503.02531, March 2015)
takeaway: Classic recipe for training a small student model on a large teacher's softened outputs; SatClip can use it to shrink a CLIP land-cover head or a question parser so it runs fast on CPU

title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
venue: Human Factors 46(1): 50-80
takeaway: Foundational review arguing that trust should match automation capability (calibrated trust), not be maximised; SatClip should design the evidence card to expose when and why instruments are reliable

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
venue: CHI 2019 (Proceedings of the 2019 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 1-13)
takeaway: 18 validated design guidelines for AI products; SatClip should use them as a checklist for its chat UI and evidence card, especially setting expectations, scoping when unsure and supporting correction

title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
venue: CHI 2021
takeaway: Explanations made people accept AI answers more often whether right or wrong, adding nothing over showing confidence alone; SatClip's VLM explanations must not make wrong numbers more persuasive

title: NL4DV: A Toolkit for Generating Analytic Specifications for Data Visualization from Natural Language Queries
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 27(2) (Proceedings of IEEE VIS 2020)
takeaway: Python toolkit that turns a natural-language data question into a structured JSON of attributes, tasks and charts, with explicit ambiguity flags; SatClip's question parser should emit a similar inspectable spec

title: Earth observation tools and services to increase the effectiveness of humanitarian assistance
venue: European Journal of Remote Sensing 53(sup2): 67-85 (published online 30 October 2019; issue dated 2020)
takeaway: Field report on delivering EO information to MSF and other NGOs, stressing that trust, reliability and workflow fit, not algorithms, limit uptake; SatClip should design around delivery and trust for non-expert responders

title: Effect of Confidence and Explanation on Accuracy and Trust Calibration in AI-Assisted Decision Making
venue: FAT* 2020 (ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency)
takeaway: Showing a confidence score helped people rely on AI more when it was confident, but did not raise joint accuracy, and SHAP explanations did not help calibration; SatClip should show calibrated confidence and treat it as a reliance aid, not an accuracy fix

title: DOTA: A Large-scale Dataset for Object Detection in Aerial Images
venue: CVPR 2018
takeaway: The standard oriented-box benchmark for aerial object detection (15 classes, very high resolution); useful context but its objects are mostly below Sentinel-2's 10 m pixel, so SatClip should not promise object counts

title: xView: Objects in Context in Overhead Imagery
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:1802.07856, February 2018)
takeaway: Over 1 million objects in 60 classes from 0.3 m WorldView-3 imagery, with a weak SSD baseline; shows how hard fine-grained small-object detection is even at 0.3 m, reinforcing that SatClip should not count objects in Sentinel data

title: Object Detection in Optical Remote Sensing Images: A Survey and A New Benchmark
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 159: 296-307
takeaway: Survey plus the DIOR benchmark (23,463 images, 20 classes, 0.5 to 30 m); a reference for mixed-resolution detection, but SatClip should cite it only to justify scoping out object-level questions

title: Oriented R-CNN for Object Detection
venue: ICCV 2021
takeaway: Simple, fast two-stage rotated-box detector (75.87% mAP on DOTA, 96.50% on HRSC2016, 15.1 FPS on a GPU); a strong baseline if SatClip ever adds ship detection, but its GPU speed does not translate to our CPU budget

title: xView3-SAR: Detecting Dark Fishing Activity Using Synthetic Aperture Radar Imagery
venue: NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv comment: accepted to NeurIPS 2022; track not confirmed by us)
takeaway: Large Sentinel-1 VV/VH ship detection benchmark (991 scenes, 243,018 labelled objects); the closest object-detection work to SatClip's own data, useful for SAR preprocessing and as a model for honest, partially reliable labels

title: GeoPixel: Pixel Grounding Large Multimodal Model in Remote Sensing
venue: ICML 2025
takeaway: First RS chat model that emits masks inside its answer; useful pattern for linking each claim to a region, but masks are about 52 mIoU so SatClip's region mask must still come from instruments

title: GeoGround: A Unified Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing Visual Grounding
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2411.11904, v3); no peer-reviewed venue found
takeaway: Shows masks can be emitted as compact text by a plain LLaVA, so even a small VLM could point at regions; but its masks are coarse and need SAM to be competitive, so keep instrument masks as the truth

title: VHM: Versatile and Honest Vision Language Model for Remote Sensing Image Analysis
venue: AAAI 2025 (arXiv:2403.20213 first posted March 2024)
takeaway: Closest prior art to SatClip's abstention: trains an RS VLM to reject questions about absent objects; but honesty is learned refusal on four question types, not calibrated confidence over measurements

title: EarthMind: Leveraging Cross-Sensor Data for Advanced Earth Observation Interpretation with a Unified Multimodal LLM
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.01667, v2); no peer-reviewed venue found
takeaway: Strongest evidence that plain VLMs ignore SAR when given SAR plus optical; supports SatClip's choice to read SAR with instruments, and EarthMind-Bench is a ready SAR-only test set

title: Falcon: A Remote Sensing Vision-Language Foundation Model (Technical Report)
venue: arXiv preprint (technical report, arXiv:2503.11070, v2); no peer-reviewed venue found
takeaway: A 0.7B RS model that does grounding, segmentation and bitemporal change detection is the most CPU-plausible RS VLM to date; worth testing as SatClip's parser/explainer or as a cross-check, never as the measuring instrument

title: Geo-R1: Improving Few-Shot Geospatial Referring Expression Understanding with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, vol. 237, 2026 (doi:10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.04.023)
takeaway: RL with verifiable rewards lets a 3B VLM learn RS grounding from about 10 examples per class, including SAR; a cheap route to adapt SatClip's parser to Indian place and crop phrases, but its SAR accuracy (25%) confirms the VLM should not measure

title: FUSAR-GPT: A Spatiotemporal Feature-Embedded and Two-Stage Decoupled Visual Language Model for SAR Imagery
venue: CVPR 2026 (poster)
takeaway: Injecting location-keyed AlphaEarth embeddings lifts a 7B SAR VLM by 7 to 12 points, a hint that SatClip could add a precomputed geospatial prior; but its own counting accuracy is about 53% on a small test set, so SAR answers still need instruments

title: Sentinel-1-based flood mapping: a fully automated processing chain
venue: International Journal of Remote Sensing 37(13), pp. 2990-3004
takeaway: Blueprint for sar_water_otsu: pick bimodal, darker-than-average tiles, threshold them, then refine with slope, size and HAND fuzzy rules; VV is slightly better than VH in calm wind

title: Towards operational near real-time flood detection using a split-based automatic thresholding procedure on high resolution TerraSAR-X data
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences 9(2), pp. 303-314
takeaway: Origin of tile-wise SAR flood thresholding: only threshold tiles whose variability and darkness indicate both water and land, then pool their histograms

title: A fully automated TerraSAR-X based flood service
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 104, pp. 203-212
takeaway: Proof that unsupervised tile thresholding plus fuzzy refinement survives 175 real flood scenes worldwide, including tropical Thailand; the robustness tricks matter more than the threshold rule

title: A hierarchical split-based approach for parametric thresholding of SAR images: Flood inundation as a test case
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (2017; listed as early access, pp. 1-14, on the LIST record; final volume and issue not confirmed)
takeaway: Use Ashman D > 2 plus a 10% minority-class rule as SatClip's explicit bimodality check, searching tiles of variable size rather than a fixed grid

title: SEN12MS-CR-TS: A Remote Sensing Data Set for Multi-modal Multi-temporal Cloud Removal
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (per the arXiv version; volume and article number not confirmed)
takeaway: A year of co-registered S1/S2 time series with real clouds: shows that several cloudy dates plus SAR beat one date, and that very cloudy (>90%) cases stay hard

title: UnCRtainTS: Uncertainty Quantification for Cloud Removal in Optical Satellite Time Series
venue: CVPR 2023 Workshops (EarthVision), pp. 2086-2096
takeaway: Calibrated per-pixel variance lets you discard the most uncertain half of outputs and nearly halve error; the same rank-and-reject logic is SatClip's abstain rule

title: Change-Agent: Towards Interactive Comprehensive Remote Sensing Change Interpretation and Analysis
venue: IEEE TGRS
takeaway: Closest prior art to SatClip's 'instrument as eyes, LLM as brain' split for change questions, but the LLM writes free Python and nothing is calibrated, receipted or allowed to abstain

title: GeoGPT: Understanding and Processing Geospatial Tasks through An Autonomous GPT
venue: arXiv preprint
takeaway: Early GIS tool agent that openly reports run-to-run instability and hallucinated file and tool arguments; its tool-side input validation is a cheap guard SatClip should copy for every instrument

title: Autonomous GIS: the next-generation AI-powered GIS
venue: International Journal of Digital Earth
takeaway: Influential vision of an LLM that generates, verifies and runs its own GIS workflows; SatClip deliberately takes the opposite, non-generative path and should cite this as the alternative it rejects for reliability

title: ThinkGeo: Evaluating Tool-Augmented Agents for Remote Sensing Tasks
venue: arXiv preprint (GitHub README lists CVPR 2026 MONTI workshop; not confirmed on a proceedings page)
takeaway: RS tool-agent benchmark where even GPT-4o gets tool arguments right only about a third of the time and final answers right under 10% end to end; the strongest published case for SatClip's fixed instruments and exact tool-call scoring

title: GeoBenchX: Benchmarking LLMs in Agent Solving Multistep Geospatial Tasks
venue: 1st ACM SIGSPATIAL International Workshop on Generative and Agentic AI for Multi-Modality Space-Time Intelligence (GeoGenAgent 2025)
takeaway: Only geo-agent benchmark here that scores refusal on deliberately unsolvable tasks; shows models trade answering for refusing, which supports SatClip's explicit abstention and gives a test design to copy

title: Earth-Agent: Unlocking the Full Landscape of Earth Observation with Agents
venue: ICLR 2026
takeaway: Most capable EO tool agent to date (104 MCP tools, spectral indices, GEE products) and the closest competitor to SatClip's instrument idea, yet GPT-5 matches tool parameters only about 26% of the time and there is no calibration, abstention or receipt

title: Earth AI: Unlocking Geospatial Insights with Foundation Models and Cross-Modal Reasoning
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2510.18318, multiple revisions; also listed on research.google)
takeaway: The closest big-tech threat: a Gemini agent that chains Google's imagery, population and flood models into answers, but with no abstention, no per-answer scene receipts and an RGB-high-res imagery focus; SatClip must win on transparent instruments, refusal and auditability

title: AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2507.22291, v1 29 July 2025, v2 8 September 2025)
takeaway: Precomputed annual 10 m embeddings for every land pixel make cheap land-cover and change features available to anyone, a strong optional baseline for SatClip, but annual, opaque and not usable for a specific flood date

title: TerraMind: Large-Scale Generative Multimodality for Earth Observation
venue: ICCV 2025 (arXiv:2504.11171, v1 15 April 2025, latest v5 June 2026)
takeaway: Open Apache-2.0 any-to-any model over Sentinel-1/2, DEM, LULC and NDVI with strong water mapping; a candidate fine-tuned instrument or cross-check for SatClip, but its generated 'imagined' modalities must never feed evidence-card numbers

title: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission and data products
venue: Satellite mission (launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota); ASF NISAR data documentation
takeaway: Free L-band and S-band SAR with a 12-day repeat, provisional calibrated products since July 2026 and S-band samples on ISRO Bhoonidhi; L-band sees flooding under crop canopy, an obvious next instrument for SatClip once access and format are wired in

title: 2026 IEEE GRSS Data Fusion Contest: SAR Temporal Storytelling
venue: IEEE GRSS Data Fusion Contest (results at IGARSS 2026, Washington DC; papers planned for IGARSS 2026 Proceedings and IEEE JSTARS)
takeaway: The field's flagship 2026 contest asked teams to turn SAR time series into readable stories of change, validating SatClip's framing; but entries were open-ended research on commercial X-band, not abstaining, receipted answers on free data

title: Copernicus Sentinel-1D launch and restored two-satellite Sentinel-1 constellation (Sentinel-1C and 1D)
venue: ESA press release and Copernicus Sentinels success story (mission announcement)
takeaway: Sentinel-1C (Dec 2024) plus 1D (Nov 2025) restore two-satellite C-band SAR, about 6-day revisit at the equator, which directly raises how often SatClip can answer a flood question with a fresh scene instead of abstaining

title: Bhuvan: ISRO's Geoportal (Gateway to Indian Earth Observation)
venue: Official geoportal and brochure, NRSC/ISRO, Hyderabad (portal launched 2009); OGC blog profile by Divya Khanna, 7 Feb 2025
takeaway: Bhuvan is the map Indian officials already know, so SatClip should publish its evidence-card masks as OGC-compatible layers that overlay on Bhuvan rather than ask users to switch platforms

title: National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM): Web enabled Geospatial Portal
venue: NRSC brochure for NDEM version 3.0, April 2017, Hyderabad
takeaway: NDEM is the official channel through which district disaster managers already receive NRSC flood inundation maps, so SatClip must position as a fast, auditable complement and export in formats NDEM users can ingest

title: Yield Estimation System based on Technology (YES-TECH) under PMFBY: Manual for Implementation
venue: Official manual, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, New Delhi, January 2023
takeaway: YES-TECH makes satellite crop masks and modelled yields legally count for 30 percent of insurance loss assessment, and it lists Sentinel-1 and EOS-04 backscatter as inputs, so SatClip's agriculture answers should be framed at insurance unit level with explicit validation

title: Analysis of Wheat Crop Forecasts, in India, Generated Using Remote Sensing Data, under FASAL Project
venue: Int. Arch. Photogramm. Remote Sens. Spatial Inf. Sci., XLII-3/W6: 223-228 (ISPRS-GEOGLAM-ISRS workshop, New Delhi, Feb 2019)
takeaway: India's official crop forecasting already compares satellite area estimates with government statistics by deviation, RMSE and correlation at district level, so SatClip should validate its agriculture instrument the same way and report the deviation on the evidence card

title: Large-Scale Flood Hazard Monitoring and Impact Assessment on Landscape: Representative Case Study in India
venue: Sustainability (MDPI), 15(14): 11413
takeaway: A peer-reviewed Assam 2022 Sentinel-1 study reports a flooded area of about 33,900 km2 (43 percent of the state) with no stated uncertainty, which is exactly the kind of headline number SatClip should reproduce with scene IDs, a confidence and an abstention rule

title: Flood Hazard Zonation Atlas of Assam: Using multi-sensor satellite data (1998-2023)
venue: NRSC technical report NRSC-RSA-DMSG-FMHAD-MAY,2025-TR-2791, Version 3, June 2025
takeaway: NRSC's official Assam atlas classifies every 50 m pixel and village by how many times it flooded in 26 years, giving SatClip both a prior for plausibility checks and the hazard vocabulary district officials already use

title: Operational Near Real Time Rice Area Mapping Using Multi-Temporal Sentinel-1 SAR Observations
venue: Int. Arch. Photogramm. Remote Sens. Spatial Inf. Sci., XLII-4: 433-438 (ISPRS TC IV Mid-term Symposium, Delft, Oct 2018)
takeaway: Kharif rice in coastal Andhra Pradesh can be mapped from Sentinel-1 alone with about 84 percent independent accuracy, and accuracy rises as each new monsoon acquisition arrives, so SatClip's sown-area answers should state how many SAR dates they used and abstain early in the season

title: A Threshold Selection Method from Gray-Level Histograms
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics, 9(1): 62-66
takeaway: The default automatic threshold that SatClip must benchmark Kittler-Illingworth against, and a cheap fallback when the two-Gaussian fit fails

title: Minimum error thresholding
venue: Pattern Recognition, 19(1): 41-47
takeaway: The core of SatClip's SAR water instrument: fit two Gaussians to the gamma0 dB histogram and pick the Bayes minimum error threshold, with the criterion value doubling as a quality check

title: The use of the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) in the delineation of open water features
venue: International Journal of Remote Sensing, 17(7): 1425-1432
takeaway: Gives SatClip its optical water instrument, (Green minus NIR) over (Green plus NIR) on Sentinel-2 B3 and B8, used only on cloud-free, shadow-masked pixels as a cross-check on SAR

title: Red and photographic infrared linear combinations for monitoring vegetation
venue: Remote Sensing of Environment, 8(2): 127-150
takeaway: The foundation of SatClip's NDVI-difference instrument: red and NIR combinations track green biomass, so NDVI change between clear dates is a defensible crop-damage signal

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 16(1): 41-46
takeaway: The theoretical root of SatClip's abstention: reject when the best posterior falls below a threshold, and choose that threshold from the error-reject curve rather than by feel

title: Digital Image Enhancement and Noise Filtering by Use of Local Statistics
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, PAMI-2(2): 165-168
takeaway: The Lee filter is the cheap, explainable speckle reducer SatClip should apply to gamma0 before thresholding, with window size logged in the receipt

title: Change Vector Analysis: An Approach for Detecting Forest Changes with Landsat
venue: LARS Symposia (Symposium on Machine Processing of Remotely Sensed Data, Purdue University), paper 385; pages not confirmed
takeaway: Origin of change vector analysis: describe change as magnitude plus direction in a transformed feature space, which lets SatClip say what kind of change happened, not just that something changed

title: EarthVQA: Towards Queryable Earth via Relational Reasoning-Based Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2024)
takeaway: Even a VQA model that is fed segmentation masks scores far lower on counting and comprehensive analysis than on yes/no judging, which backs SatClip's choice to compute counts and areas from masks and let the language model only phrase them

title: RSVG: Exploring Data and Models for Visual Grounding on Remote Sensing Data
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 61: 1-13
takeaway: DIOR-RSVG is the standard test for pointing at a named object in a scene, and its failure modes (clutter, ambiguous phrases) show why SatClip should ground questions to an administrative polygon, not to a model-predicted box

title: XLRS-Bench: Could Your Multimodal LLMs Understand Extremely Large Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery?
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2025)
takeaway: On huge real scenes the best MLLMs average about 40% on four-option questions and almost never draw a correct box, so SatClip should tile scenes and measure with instruments rather than ask a VLM to read a whole Sentinel scene

title: DisasterM3: A Remote Sensing Vision-Language Dataset for Disaster Damage Assessment and Response
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (acceptance stated in the project README)
takeaway: The closest benchmark to SatClip's use case: general and RS VLMs score barely above chance on disaster damage counting and degrade on SAR, which is direct support for SatClip's instrument-first, SAR-first, VLM-explains-only design

title: GEO-Bench: Toward Foundation Models for Earth Monitoring
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)
takeaway: GEO-Bench's evaluation protocol (many seeds, interquartile mean, bootstrapped confidence intervals) is the template SatClip should follow when it reports any instrument accuracy, and its finding that RS pre-training often did not beat ImageNet weights warns against assuming a geo model is better

title: PANGAEA: A Global and Inclusive Benchmark for Geospatial Foundation Models
venue: arXiv preprint 2412.04204; published as PANGAEA: Assessing Geospatial Foundation Models Capabilities through a Global and Inclusive Benchmark, IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine, 14(1): 245-285 (2026)
takeaway: On Sen1Floods11 a plain supervised UNet beats every geospatial foundation model and RemoteCLIP reaches only about 55 water IoU, so SatClip should keep classical SAR thresholding as its water instrument and not swap in a foundation model or RemoteCLIP for flood extent

title: The openEO API: Harmonising the Use of Earth Observation Cloud Services Using Virtual Data Cube Functionalities
venue: Remote Sensing (MDPI), 13(6): 1125
takeaway: openEO is the standard way to push a SatClip instrument to a backend such as Copernicus Data Space as a portable process graph, so SatClip should keep its instruments expressible as data cube steps and record that graph in the receipt

title: CEOS-ARD Product Family Specification: Synthetic Aperture Radar (Normalised Radar Backscatter [NRB], Polarimetric Radar, Ocean Radar Backscatter, Geocoded SLC, Interferometric Radar, Composite Backscatter), Version 1.3.1
venue: CEOS Analysis Ready Data Product Family Specification, v1.3.1 (July 2026); successor to CARD4L NRB PFS v5.5
takeaway: CEOS-ARD NRB is the checklist for what a trustworthy gamma0 RTC input looks like (data mask with layover and shadow, local incidence angle, scattering area, DEM provenance), and SatClip should record which of these its RTC source supplies on every evidence card

title: Sentinel 1 Radiometrically Terrain Corrected (RTC), Microsoft Planetary Computer dataset (STAC collection sentinel-1-rtc)
venue: Microsoft Planetary Computer dataset catalogue and STAC API (official documentation)
takeaway: Planetary Computer's sentinel-1-rtc is the most direct source of the gamma0 RTC that SatClip's SAR instruments need, but it is flagged account-required and ships only vv and vh, so SatClip must treat token failure as a normal failover case and derive its own shadow mask

title: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem documentation: STAC product catalogue, OData catalogue and S3 access APIs
venue: Official online documentation, documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu
takeaway: CDSE is SatClip's authoritative last-resort catalogue: its new STAC 1.1 endpoint and OData API index every Sentinel product, but pixel access needs S3 credentials and products are mostly SAFE archives, so it is the slowest and most fragile of the three failover routes

title: odc-stac: Load STAC items into xarray Datasets (Open Data Cube)
venue: Open-source Python library, PyPI odc-stac (first release Aug 2021; v0.5.3 current on 2026-10-06), documentation at odc-stac.readthedocs.io
takeaway: odc-stac turns a STAC search result into a district-clipped, grid-aligned xarray cube with windowed COG reads, which is close to exactly SatClip's data layer, so SatClip should reuse it (with patch_url for signing and fail_on_error off) rather than hand-roll reprojection and mosaicking

title: Probabilities for SV Machines
venue: Chapter in Advances in Large-Margin Classifiers (eds. Smola, Bartlett, Schoelkopf, Schuurmans), MIT Press, 2000; widely cited as a 1999 technical report titled Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines and Comparisons to Regularized Likelihood Methods
takeaway: Platt scaling is the simplest way to turn a raw SatClip score (for example a backscatter margin below the Otsu threshold) into a probability, and is the baseline any fancier calibrator must beat

title: Transforming classifier scores into accurate multiclass probability estimates
venue: Proceedings of the Eighth ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD 2002), pp. 694-699
takeaway: Isotonic regression is SatClip's default non-parametric calibrator for instrument scores once there are enough labelled tiles, since it assumes only that a higher score should never mean a lower flood probability

title: Obtaining Well Calibrated Probabilities Using Bayesian Binning
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 29(1) (AAAI 2015)
takeaway: Gives SatClip the ECE and MCE metrics for checking that a stated 0.80 confidence is right about 80 percent of the time, plus a binning calibrator that averages over bin choices

title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
venue: NeurIPS 2017 (NIPS 2017)
takeaway: Running several independently varied instrument settings and reporting their spread is a cheap, model-agnostic way for SatClip to widen confidence when the instruments disagree

title: What Uncertainties Do We Need in Bayesian Deep Learning for Computer Vision?
venue: NeurIPS 2017 (NIPS 2017)
takeaway: SatClip should separate uncertainty from the sensor (speckle, cloud, mixed pixels, which more data cannot fix) from uncertainty from the method (thresholds tuned elsewhere, which local labels can fix), and say which one caused an abstention

title: Local Temperature Scaling for Probability Calibration
venue: ICCV 2021 (arXiv comment: Accepted by ICCV-2021; first posted August 2020)
takeaway: Calibration for SatClip's flood masks should be allowed to vary across the tile (river channels, hill shadow, urban areas), not a single global temperature, and must leave the mask itself unchanged

title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
venue: NeurIPS 2019
takeaway: A calibration fitted on one region or season will drift when SatClip meets a new district or an unusual monsoon, so calibration must be re-checked per region and season, and confidence should fall as inputs move away from the calibration data

title: Conformal Risk Control
venue: ICLR 2024 (spotlight); arXiv first posted August 2022
takeaway: Lets SatClip pick its flood-mask threshold from labelled Indian events so that the expected share of truly flooded area it misses stays below a stated level, with a finite-sample guarantee

title: Visual Semiotics & Uncertainty Visualization: An Empirical Study
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 18(12): 2496-2505 (Proceedings of IEEE VIS 2012)
takeaway: Map uncertainty symbols are not equally intuitive, so SatClip's map overlay should encode low-confidence or cloud-masked pixels with a symbol type users read correctly at a glance, tested with real officials rather than chosen by the developer

title: When (ish) is My Bus? User-centered Visualizations of Uncertainty in Everyday, Mobile Predictive Systems
venue: CHI 2016 (Proceedings of the 2016 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, pp. 5092-5103)
takeaway: Non-experts on a phone read uncertainty best as a small number of countable discrete outcomes, so SatClip's confidence meter and flooded-area range should use a frequency framing (for example 20 dots) instead of a density curve or a bare percentage

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 5(CSCW1), pp. 1-21 (CSCW 2021)
takeaway: Making users commit to their own guess or ask for the AI answer reduces blind acceptance but is disliked, so SatClip could offer an optional 'check it yourself first' step for high-stakes cards and should keep the default card fast

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 7(CSCW1), pp. 1-38 (CSCW 2023)
takeaway: Explanations only cut overreliance when they make checking the AI cheaper than trusting it, so SatClip's evidence (scene chips, before/after thumbnails) must let an official verify the headline number in seconds

title: Global trends in satellite-based emergency mapping
takeaway: Satellite emergency mapping is already routine for Asian disasters, but delivered as expert map products; SatClip's niche is turning the same evidence into a fast, honest answer card that non-experts can act on, with clear limits

title: Eviza: A Natural Language Interface for Visual Analysis
venue: UIST 2016 (Proceedings of the 29th Annual Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, pp. 365-377)
takeaway: When a question is ambiguous (which district, which date, what counts as flooded), SatClip should show the default it chose as an editable chip, as Eviza's ambiguity widgets do, rather than silently guessing or refusing

title: Automatic analysis of the difference image for unsupervised change detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 38(3): 1171-1182
takeaway: The template for SatClip's two-date change instruments: model the difference image as a changed and unchanged mixture fitted by EM, pick the minimum-error Bayes threshold, and reuse the fitted posteriors as the confidence that drives abstention

title: Change Detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar Images Based on Deep Neural Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 27(1): 125-138
takeaway: An early, influential case for learning SAR change directly from the image pair instead of a log-ratio; for SatClip it is a cross-check idea, not a replacement, because it trades away the transparent, auditable difference image

title: Fully Convolutional Siamese Networks for Change Detection
venue: 2018 25th IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), Athens, pp. 4063-4067
takeaway: The standard small learned baseline for Sentinel-2 change (FC-EF, FC-Siam-conc, FC-Siam-diff); its modest OSCD F1 near 58 percent shows learned 10 m change maps are far from reliable enough to be SatClip's reported number

title: A Transformer-Based Siamese Network for Change Detection
venue: IGARSS 2022, IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium, pp. 207-210
takeaway: A widely used learned CD baseline whose large DSIFN gain comes from a 192-patch test set on very high resolution imagery; a reminder that benchmark F1 says little about 10 m Sentinel change and cannot stand in for SatClip's calibrated instruments

title: Segment Any Change
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, pp. 81204-81224)
takeaway: Zero-shot foundation-model change detection is real but low precision (roughly 4 to 31 percent pixel precision across four benchmarks, with high recall); SatClip could use it to propose candidate change regions, never to report a changed area

title: Detecting trend and seasonal changes in satellite image time series
venue: Remote Sensing of Environment, 114(1): 106-115
takeaway: Seasonality alone can masquerade as change in a two-date NDVI difference; SatClip's crop-change instrument should compare against the same season's expected NDVI and abstain when a drop could be ordinary phenology or harvest

title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
venue: ICLR 2023 (arXiv October 2022)
takeaway: A one-shot, calibration-based 3 to 4-bit weight quantizer to benchmark against AWQ when shrinking SatClip's merged 2B intent model, judged on intent-JSON accuracy rather than perplexity

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
venue: NeurIPS 2022
takeaway: Explains why naive 8-bit quantization breaks transformers (rare large outlier features) and gives a safe 8-bit baseline that SatClip's quantized builds must match on intent accuracy

title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
venue: ICML 2024 (Oral)
takeaway: A drop-in LoRA variant with no extra inference cost; worth an A/B run against plain LoRA on SatClip's question-to-intent training set before committing to one

title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model's Perception of the World at Any Resolution
venue: arXiv preprint (technical report, September 2024); no peer-reviewed venue found
takeaway: A strong open 2B VLM base whose dynamic-resolution input suits Sentinel chips of varying size, but SatClip should use it only for intent parsing and explanation, never for the numbers

title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint (July 2023); no peer-reviewed venue found
takeaway: Constrain the intent model's decoding to SatClip's JSON schema so every output parses and only allowed fields and values can appear, at little extra cost on CPU
